To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a monolithic, 3-axis, MEMS magnetometer with a noise floor of 100nT/Hz and a full-scale range from ±1mT to ±7mT, with a 3-axis cross-axis contribution of less than 1%.

(i) we designed, fabricated, and tested a monolithic 3-axis MEMS multi-loop Lorentz-force-based magnetometer that is the first of its kind in the literature; (ii) the sensor is fabricated on a single chip with a footprint of 0.5 mm2, and it includes three current recirculation paths to sense the magnetic field along three axes; (iii) we developed and tested the first MEMS-based oscillator to drive the sensor; (iv)
the sensor reaches on the three axes a noise level of 100 n T /√Hz over a 3-dB 50-Hz bandwidth, with a 0.1 % nonlinearity and a full-scale range ± 7 m T.

the design and implementation of a novel monolithic 3-axis MEMS magnetometer.

it is possible to design a monolithic 3-axis Lorentz-force sensor that combines the sensitivity of a separate-axis sensor with the footprint of a single-axis sensor.
the performance of the 3-axis sensor is comparable to that of the single-axis sensor.
